newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-OREGON LUMBERMAN WAS TOP BIDDER FOR STORM CAT COLT.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-OREGON LUMBERMAN WAS TOP BIDDER FOR STORM CAT COLT.

text.p: Bob Baffert, the trainer of Silver Charm, winner of this year's Kentucky Derby and Preakness, cleared up a day-old mystery on Wednesday by identifying the man who paid $1.5 million for a Storm Cat colt.

Baffert said that Aaron Jones, a Oregon lumberman, called him in Lexington on Sunday and asked him to "pick out a horse that could take him to the Derby," said Baffert. "He said it looked like I was having a lot of fun. He wants a good horse and he wants to have fun."

Baffert was on the phone with Jones throughout the bidding on Tuesday. "I lost him at $600,000," Baffert said. "The phone connection went. I called him back. I didn't know if he wanted me to bid beyond $1 million but he was a game guy and said 'don't let him go!'"
Jones, from Eugene, Oregon, has been involved for years with thoroughbreds, but sold them years ago after feeling, said Baffert, "he was having no luck and no fun."
Minutes after he signed the sales ticket Tuesday, Baffert learned that the underbidder was Bob Lewis, owner of Silver Charm.
"I didn't want anyone to know what I was trying to buy. Neither did Bob Lewis," Baffert said on Wednesday. "So I didn't know he was the underbidder."
